mechanism: FERC non-capacity license amendment on the delegated-authority track, Bradley Lake Expansion / Dixon Diversion, Project No. P-8221-124

sources.story_title: NEWS TRIGGER + acceptance and standing layer. Notice of application for non-capacity amendment of license accepted for filing, Project No. P-8221-124. Carries the verbatim project description, the 38 percent generation figure, the 5:00 p.m. ET 28 August 2026 intervention deadline, and the standing rule.

CHOKEPOINT layer. Delegations to the Director of the Office of Energy Projects. Paragraph (b) authorizes the Director or the Director's designee to take appropriate action on uncontested applications for amendments to Part I Federal Power Act licenses.

Licensee filing layer. Bradley Lake Expansion Project page. Final License Amendment Application filed with FERC 30 June 2026; construction cost approximately 400 million dollars; construction funding source yet to be determined; roughly three years of study and permitting followed by three years of construction.

Project governance layer. BPMC consists of AEA and the five purchaser utilities (Chugach, Golden Valley, Homer, Matanuska, Seward Electric) and is responsible for management, operation, maintenance and improvement of the project, subject to AEA's non-delegable duties.

Financing framework layer. Release index confirms 'AEA Files Final Amendment Application for Bradley Lake Expansion Project' (20 July 2026) and 'AEA Board Advances Financing Framework for Bradley Lake Expansion Project' (23 July 2026).

In-window trade coverage of the AEA board financing action. Source of the Clay Koplin board-chair attribution and of the 1.5 Bcf per year gas-displacement and 2031 in-service figures, all of which are SECONDARY and were not confirmed against a primary source.
